mainText:
A major vegetation fire near Queenstown has surged to twelve hundred hectares as strong winds fuel the flames, with firefighters expecting further growth today.

New Zealand.

A bush fire on Walter Peak, on the shores of Lake Wakatipu near Queenstown, has grown to twelve hundred hectares. Firefighters suspended operations on Tuesday night when it was neither contained nor controlled, and crews returned about seven this morning with strong winds forecast to keep pushing it further. The Crown has confirmed it will not seek a retrial of David Tamihere over the 1990 murders of Swedish backpackers Sven Hoglin and Heidi Paakkonen, six months after the Supreme Court quashed his convictions. A new poll shows National and Labour both stuck in the twenties, with the Opportunity Party holding the balance of power, as analysts pick over Tuesday night's first leaders debate between Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins. Labour has admitted a small ninety million dollar error in its costings after National's Nicola Willis challenged its Investment Boost numbers, but says its commitments are still fully funded. Police say a major re-investigation under Operation Hark has uncovered eleven further cases of alleged offending after initial reports were not properly followed up, with two men now charged with sexual offending as a result. Petrol prices have hit their highest level since the start of the Iran war, adding to what RNZ describes as three tough knocks on consumer spending alongside rates and weather, with Paymark data showing spending below last year's levels.

In the Bay of Plenty, a man who stabbed a friend to death after a party, Dallas Hohua, has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years. Western Bay of Plenty's byelection process continues after councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision.

World.

Rwanda-backed rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with residents reporting gunfire and shelling after Congolese troops were overrun. The United Nations estimates more than one million displaced people are now inside the city. Palestinians have begun streaming back on foot into northern Gaza after Israel allowed crossings through a military zone bisecting the enclave, following a deadlock over hostage releases. Hamas has released four more female Israeli hostages under the ceasefire deal, with ninety one hostages still held, including the bodies of at least thirty four. Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola death, a man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than four thousand people have died in the worst outbreak in that country's history. A suspected sabotage of a deep sea cable in the Baltic Sea has triggered NATO's first coordinated response to attacks on undersea infrastructure, after another cable was severed.

Technology.

OpenAI has told a hearing that its response to hacks of Australian government systems was, in its own words, not good enough, with executive Jason Kwon saying the company has since added more precautions to its training environments. The Pentagon has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools altogether after blacklisting the company in February as a supply chain risk, when Anthropic refused to strip safety guardrails from its systems. Asos has confirmed hackers sent an unauthorised notification to users through its app, and is telling customers not to engage with the message while it investigates further.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks have called up two experienced forwards to add power to the pack for the Bledisloe Cup test against the Wallabies at Eden Park, with assistant coach Tana Umaga saying the team's three test losing streak sticks in the guts. Hurricanes first-five Ruben Love is out for the rest of the year after ankle surgery. The National Provincial Championship quarter-finalists are set, with Canterbury rising up the table and Wellington finishing with the wooden spoon. Kalyn Ponga will make his Kiwis debut and Stacey Waaka becomes a dual international, both named in New Zealand's Rugby League World Cup squads.

Swimming. Lewis Clareburt has broken two national records at a World Cup meet in Azerbaijan, with Clareburt and Caitlin Deans both producing times that qualify for next year's world championships.

Cricket. Black Caps veteran Michael Bracewell has moved to a casual contract, giving up his New Zealand Cricket central deal. India has recalled seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar for the Twenty20 series against the Black Caps, his first call up in four years, on the back of a strong Indian Premier League season.

Tennis. Novak Djokovic has won the China Open, his hundred and second career title, after Alex de Minaur retired injured in the final. Carlos Alcaraz won the Japan Open, his third tour title of the year. American Brandon Nakashima has signed up for January's ASB Classic in Auckland, the second top twenty player to commit after last year's champion Jakub Mensik.

Football. The All Whites lost two one to Japan in Tokyo in the Kirin Cup, spending much of the match defending their own penalty box.

No Super Rugby or Warriors fixtures.

Coming up. The Bledisloe Cup test between the All Blacks and Wallabies is at Eden Park. The Western Bay of Plenty byelection process continues following Alan Kurtovich's resignation. Campaign coverage continues ahead of the election.

End of flash.
